rules.title: Application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee no higher than the actual out-of-pocket cost of screening you, and never more than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI increases since 1998. Ask for the current CPI-adjusted figure if you are charged more than $30.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually since 1998, and no more than actual out-of-pocket costs

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in California; applicants include guarantors and cosigners.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Does not preempt deposit and fee rules of federal or state housing assistance programs

rules.exemptions: Section does not preempt fee rules under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.interaction: Latest amendment: Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026; the original start date of the cap is not stated in the text. CPI adjustments began January 1, 1998.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge you a screening fee if they know or should know that no unit is available now or within a reasonable time.

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in California.

rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.interaction: Section last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Screening fee allowed only with first-come process or refund to unselected applicants
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if they either consider complete applications in order received under written criteria (approving the first qualified applicant and charging only when your application is actually considered, refunding within 7 days if collected by mistake), or refund the full fee to every applicant not selected within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever is first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever first

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in California.

rules.exemptions: No refund required under the first-come option to an applicant denied after consideration for failing the screening criteria.
rules.quoted_span: An application screening process in which the landlord or their agent returns the entire screening fee to any applicant who is not selected for tenancy, regardless of the reason, within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.
rules.interaction: Section last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026; the document does not state when this requirement first took effect.

rules.title: Itemized receipt and refund of unused screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord must give you an itemized receipt (in person, by mail, or by email if agreed) showing out-of-pocket costs and time spent, and must return any part of the fee not used if no reference check or credit report was obtained.

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in California.

rules.quoted_span: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.
rules.interaction: Section last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Copy of credit report to fee-paying applicant
rules.requirement: If you paid a screening fee, the landlord must give you a copy of your consumer credit report within seven days of receiving it, by personal delivery, mail, or email.

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in California.

rules.quoted_span: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
rules.interaction: Section last amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026.

notes: Official statute text. History note shows latest amendment (AB 1170, effective 2026-01-01), which is not the start date of these rules, so effective_date left null. Section (e) refund-of-unused-fee text is wrapped across a line break, so the quoted span for that record uses subsection (d).
